prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the cleanest theory-to-experiment chain on the shortlist. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, built from ordinary electronic-structure ingredients (interlayer tunnelling between two Dirac cones), predicted a specific angle at which the bands flatten. The 2018 Jarillo-Herrero experiments then found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. A single tuning parameter now controls band width and interaction strength in a clean two-dimensional material, which for a band-structure theorist is a remarkable development. The platform has been reproduced by many groups and carried to other moire systems, and the three-person credit maps naturally onto prediction (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and demonstration (Jarillo-Herrero). Support is also the broadest on the table: all eight of us ranked it, and five placed it in the top three.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the microscopic origin of the superconductivity and of the correlated phases is still contested, so the interpretation is not fully settled, and sample-to-sample and twist-angle variation still complicate the experimental record. Attribution is also not airtight: earlier moire band-structure work (for example Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) predates Bistritzer-MacDonald, and the experimental effort involved lead student Yuan Cao and other groups (Dean and collaborators on hBN-encapsulated devices) beyond the credited names. A committee could reasonably argue that the field is still too young at about eight years from the key experiments.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked active-matter hydrodynamics (B011) first, arguing for a new class of nonequilibrium statistical physics (Vicsek, Toner-Tu, Ramaswamy), and ranked twisted bilayer graphene second, noting the unsettled pairing mechanism.
responses.response: I agree that the pairing mechanism is open and I do not dismiss it. Still, a Nobel discovery does not require a settled mechanism, since the prize recognises a finding and the platform it created. What is firmly established here is the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated states at the predicted angle. I take B011 seriously as a conceptual advance, but you yourself note that quantitative tests of the full Toner-Tu exponents remain limited and that Tu is omitted from the credit. That is a weaker experimental anchor than the one twisted bilayer graphene has, so I would keep B011 below it.

responses.point: Pearce placed topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (B026) first, as a mature, timely concept with a falsifiable HgTe confirmation, and ranked twisted bilayer graphene fourth because the superconductivity mechanism is unsettled and the Lopes dos Santos priority question is open.
responses.response: I ranked B026 second and share your view that it is mature and, arguably, overdue. Where I differ is on how much weight the credit problem carries. As you and Mehlig both note, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe effect and Zhang has died, so Kane, Mele and Molenkamp cannot cover the story cleanly, whereas for B009 a prediction plus experiment split is available. On your concern about priority, I consider Bistritzer-MacDonald the decisive prediction because it gave the quantitative magic-angle condition that guided the experiments. I would still accept B026 as a strong fallback if the committee prefers a more mature field.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks (B049) first for their originality and metrological consequence, and put twisted bilayer graphene last, saying he weighs it from outside his specialty.
responses.response: I respect that the clocks are an outstanding instrument achievement, and I accept the maturity argument. My reservation is overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, which the clock supporters, including Lindroth and Mehlig, also raise. Twisted bilayer graphene opens a new area of physics rather than refining a measurement, and I do not think an outside-specialty ranking should outweigh the breadth of its adoption across condensed matter. I would still support B049 if the committee wanted a metrology prize, but not above B009.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked twisted bilayer graphene first and noted that other moire contributors might be argued for, and that the superconducting pairing mechanism is unsettled.
responses.response: We agree on the ranking and the three names. I would add that the credit question should be settled by the discovery narrative (flat-band prediction, then correlated phases) rather than by the open pairing debate, so I would keep the citation phrased around the platform and the observed phases and avoid any claim about the superconducting mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the field mature enough, given that the pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram are unresolved.
Whether the Lopes dos Santos et al. precursor on moire bands and the contribution of Yuan Cao and other experimental groups weaken a Bistritzer-MacDonald-Jarillo-Herrero credit.
Whether B026 or B012 would face less attribution dispute than B009 once credit is examined in detail.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work is in electronic-structure theory and magnetism, and the profile documents no personal or institutional connection to the credited names of B009, B026 or B012.
